title: Her Things
summary: Weeks eleven and twelve. Lisa asks for her things back. Théo grieves on purpose, with rituals: a box, a letter, a fire, a stone. {He|She|They} {doesn't|doesn't|don't} get over her; {he|she|they} {gets|gets|get} through. No new lights; the existing ones hold him up.

screens.image: Théo's phone on the counter, a message preview, the screen cold blue.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Week eleven. A message from Lisa.

screens.image: The message on screen.

words.speaker: Lisa
words.text: Hi. Hope you're ok. Could I come get the rest of my things Saturday? I can just pick up a box at the door.

screens.image: Théo sitting very still, the warm lights in the background dimming slightly.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Twelve weeks of light, and one message turns the flat dark again.

screens.image: The Critic, suddenly bigger again by one size.

words.speaker: Critic
words.text: Answer something clever. Make her miss you. Make her sorry.

options.label: "You want her back. I know. Me too."

screens.image: Théo typing.

options.label: "Sure. Saturday at 11, I'll leave it at the door."

screens.image: An empty cardboard box in the middle of the floor. Objects around it: her mug, her plant, a scarf, a framed photo, a book, a hoodie of hers, a concert ticket, a drawing she made {him|her|them}.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Packing a box sounds simple. It isn't. Every object is a small door.

interaction.prompt: Tap a thing, then tap where it goes (or drag it there).

items.label: Her mug
items.line: She drank from this every morning for two years.

items.label: A scarf
items.line: It still smells a little of her.

items.label: A framed photo
items.line: The two of them, squinting into the sun.

items.label: A book
items.line: She never finished it. Neither did {he|she|they}.

items.label: A concert ticket
items.line: The night they missed the last train and walked home.

items.label: A drawing she made {him|her|them}
items.line: A bad drawing of a good day.

screens.image: The box, taped. The keep shelf with whatever the player kept.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Nothing is the right answer. Keeping a memory isn't holding on. Giving one away isn't forgetting.

screens.image: Marie-Clo's office, warm lamp.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: You don't have to get over her. You have to grieve her. They're different. Grief is a kind of thank-you for what you had.

screens.image: Marie-Clo handing {him|her|them} three small cards.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: Write to her. You won't send it. Three short parts. Short, Théo. This is not a novel.

screens.image: Théo at the kitchen table at night with paper and pen. Black, one candle.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: {He|She|They} {is|is|are} going to write to Lisa. {He|She|They} {is|is|are} not going to send it.

screens.image: The letter, part one, with a heading in cream.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Part one: three things you gave me that I get to keep.

interaction.placeholder: You taught me to slow down on Sundays.

screens.image: The letter, part two.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Part two: one thing that hurt. One sentence. It doesn't have to be fair.

screens.image: The letter, part three.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Part three: goodbye. One line that closes the door gently. The way she did.

screens.image: The letter folded, Théo holding it over the kitchen sink, a match in {his|her|their} other hand.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Some things are said by saying them. Some things are said by letting them go.

screens.image: The paper burning in the sink: flames, curling edges, the words going first.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The words go first. Then the paper. Then just a little smoke, and a smell like autumn.

interaction.note: If you do this for real: in a sink, away from anything that can catch fire.

screens.image: A small tin box, the letter going in, lid closing.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Some letters want to be kept. That's allowed too.

screens.image: Paper pieces falling like snow.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Small enough that the words can't find each other anymore.

screens.image: Saturday. Théo's door, the box outside it. Théo inside, back against the door.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Saturday, 11am. Théo sits on the floor on {his|her|their} side of the door. Like the first night. But not like the first night.

screens.image: Under the door: a shadow of feet, a hand lifting the box (we never see her face).

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Footsteps. The box lifts. A pause, as if she might knock.

screens.image: The door, unopened. Footsteps going down.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: She doesn't. {He|She|They} {doesn't|doesn't|don't}. That's right, for both of them.

screens.image: Théo crying quietly, but drawn with soft lines this time, light around {him|her|them} from the earlier lights.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo is sad. Properly sad. And {he|she|they} {notices|notices|notice} something new: {he|she|they} {isn't|isn't|aren't} desperate. Sad and desperate are different. Sad is just love with nowhere to go for a while.

screens.image: Théo walking out of town, a flat stone in {his|her|their} hand. The edge of the city, then a small lake with reeds. Watercolour grey-green.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: In the afternoon, {he|she|they} {walks|walks|walk} to the lake at the edge of town. Marie-Clo's idea. {He|She|They} {finds|finds|find} a flat stone.

screens.image: Close on the stone and a marker pen.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: What's the heaviest thing {he's|she's|they're} carrying? One word.

screens.image: Théo at the water's edge, arm back.

interaction.prompt: Throw the stone: drag it to the lake, or flick it upwards.

screens.image: The stone skipping once, twice, sinking. Rings spreading on the water.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Two skips. Then gone. The rings take a long time to settle. That's fine. Rings do.

screens.image: Walking back, the city lights coming on: every one of {his|her|their} lit windows on the skyline.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: On the way home, the city lights come on one by one. Théo knows which windows are {his|her|their} people.

screens.image: Café du Pont. Nadia sliding {him|her|them} a cup; on the foam, a little latte-art octopus. Nadia's light glows brighter.

words.speaker: Nadia
words.text: Rough day?

words.speaker: Théo
words.text: Rough day.

words.speaker: Nadia
words.text: On the house. Don't comment on the octopus.

screens.image: The Who Is Théo? map. A sentence at the bottom: "We were going to..."

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: One last thing. Théo has a habit of sentences that start with "we". Rewrite one so it starts with "I".

screens.image: Quest card.

interaction.title: Let go of one thing
interaction.text: Choose one ritual: write a short unsent letter (three parts, one goodbye line), throw a stone in water, or give away one object you've been keeping for the wrong reasons.
